models.name: discussion_board_configs
models.description: System-wide configuration settings for the discussion board. Contains key-value pairs defining behavioral limits and policies that govern posting, commenting, file uploads, moderation actions, and report handling. Managed by administrators through external tools, not by end users.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for the configuration parameter. Examples: "max_file_size_per_post_mb", "allowed_image_types", "min_post_title_length".

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: String representation of the configuration value. Can be JSON-encoded for complex values (e.g., array of string types).

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable explanation of what this configuration controls and its intended purpose.

plainFields.name: category
plainFields.description: Grouping for related configuration settings. Examples: "media", "content", "moderation", "session".

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was last modified.

models.name: discussion_board_citizens
models.description: Main entity representing a citizen user in the discussion board system. Each citizen can create posts, comments, and attach files. Requires email verification to post or commenting. This table stores authentication credentials and basic profile information for citizen users.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for authentication and notifications. Must be verified before posting or commenting.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for authentication. Never stored in plain text. Required for login functionality.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the user has verified their email address. When false, the user cannot create posts or comments.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the citizen account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the citizen account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the citizen account was soft-deleted (if applicable). Nullable since account deletion is not a required feature.

models.name: discussion_board_citizen_sessions
models.description: Session tracking table for citizen users. Each record represents one active or expired authentication session for a citizen. Follows exact mandatory schema for actor session tables with no additional fields. Managed exclusively through the authentication system, not directly by users.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: References the citizen user who owns this session. {@link discussion_board_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL where the user accessed the system during this session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL indicating the source of this session (e.g., which page linked to the login).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expired or was invalidated. Nullable since active sessions have no expiration.

models.name: discussion_board_moderators
models.description: Main entity representing a moderator user in the discussion board system. Each moderator has elevated permissions to edit, delete, and moderate content. Requires email verification. This table stores authentication credentials and basic profile information for moderator users.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for authentication and notifications. Must be verified before moderating content.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for authentication. Never stored in plain text. Required for login functionality.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the moderator has verified their email address. When false, the moderator cannot perform moderation actions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was soft-deleted (if applicable). Nullable since account deletion is not a required feature.

models.name: discussion_board_moderator_sessions
models.description: Session tracking table for moderator users. Each record represents one active or expired authentication session for a moderator. Follows exact mandatory schema for actor session tables with no additional fields. Managed exclusively through the authentication system, not directly by users.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: References the moderator user who owns this session. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL where the user accessed the system during this session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL indicating the source of this session (e.g., which page linked to the login).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expired or was invalidated. Nullable since active sessions have no expiration.

models.name: discussion_board_posts
models.description: Core discussion board posts created by citizens or moderated by administrators. Posts have independent lifecycles with versioning through status changes. This is a primary entity that must be independently searchable, browsable, and manageable. Foreign keys reference existing citizen and moderator tables for ownership and moderation actions. No denormalized fields are included; derived counts must be computed via joins or materialized views when necessary.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Creator of the post. {@link discussion_board_citizens.id}.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator who last modified this post through deletion or editing. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}. Null if no moderator action taken.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Title of the discussion post. Minimum 5 characters required by business rules.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Content body of the discussion post. Minimum 10 characters required by business rules.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current state of the post. Values: "active" (visible), "deleted_by_author" (soft-deleted by creator), "removed_by_moderator" (removed by moderator for policy violation), "pending_moderation" (under review after report).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post was initially created. Always set at creation and never modified.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post was last edited or modified. Updated when citizen edits within 24 hours or moderator edits at any time.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post was deleted or removed. NULL if active. Used for soft delete and audit trail purposes.

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description: User comments on discussion board posts. Comments are primary entities requiring independent management, search, and filtering. Each comment is associated with a specific post and authored by either a citizen or moderator. Comments have a character limit of 1,000 and display in chronological order. When deleted by a moderator or author, the content is replaced with a system message while preserving authorship and timestamp for audit purposes. Uses polymorphic ownership pattern with author_type field to distinguish between citizen and moderator authors.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_post_id
foreignFields.description: The post this comment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: author_id
foreignFields.description: The ID of the user who created this comment. Can be either a citizen or moderator. Use author_type to determine which table to reference. {@link discussion_board_citizens.id} if author_type is "citizen", {@link discussion_board_moderators.id} if author_type is "moderator".

plainFields.name: author_type
plainFields.description: The type of user who authored this comment. Must be either "citizen" or "moderator". This discriminates which subtype table contains the actor-specific details.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: The content of the comment. Must be between 1 and 1,000 characters as per requirements. Never null due to minimum character constraint.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The current status of the comment. Values: "active" (normal state), "deleted_by_moderator" (removed by moderator with [Deleted by moderator] message), "deleted_by_author" (removed by original author with [Deleted by author] message). Used to control visibility and moderation actions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was originally created. Required for chronological display and audit trail. Always present.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was last updated (e.g., edited). Required for tracking modifications and display of [Edited] marker.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was soft-deleted by a moderator or author. Nullable because comments are not always deleted. Used for audit purposes to track deletion history.

models.name: discussion_board_attachments
models.description: File attachments associated with posts on the discussion board. Each attachment represents a single file uploaded by a citizen, with metadata for file type, size, and moderation status. Attachments are managed independently by moderators who can view, download, and remove them, replacing links with [Attachment removed by moderator]. This table stores the physical file reference and metadata while supporting audit trails through soft deletion. Associated with discussion_board_posts via foreign key.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_post_id
foreignFields.description: Post that this attachment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_posts.id}.

plainFields.name: filename
plainFields.description: Original name of the uploaded file. Examples: "photo.jpg", "document.pdf". This is the filename as provided by the user during upload.

plainFields.name: filetype
plainFields.description: File extension indicating the type of uploaded file. Must be one of: jpeg, png, gif, pdf, txt, docx. This field is used for content-type validation during upload and to determine display behavior.

plainFields.name: filesize
plainFields.description: Size of the file in bytes. Maximum allowed size is 5,000,000 bytes (5 MB) per file. Used to enforce upload limits and storage calculations.

plainFields.name: storage_path
plainFields.description: Server-specific path where the file is stored. Typically a URL or filesystem path that the application can use to serve the file when requested. This is generated by the system upon successful upload.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the attachment. Values: 'active', 'removed'. Initial state is 'active'. When a moderator removes an attachment, status changes to 'removed' and the file link is replaced with [Attachment removed by moderator]. This enables soft deletion while preserving audit trail.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was first uploaded. Automatically generated by the system when the file completes upload. Follows ISO 8601 format.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was last modified. For attachments, this usually corresponds to when the status was changed from 'active' to 'removed'.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was marked as removed by a moderator. Nullable because active attachments have not been deleted. Used for audit trail and historical tracking of removal actions.

models.name: discussion_board_reports
models.description: Main entity for all reported content. This table contains shared attributes for reports initiated by either citizens or moderators. The actor_type field identifies which subtype table contains the specific actor information. This structure follows the Polymorphic Ownership Pattern to ensure database-level referential integrity and eliminate nullable foreign key anti-patterns. Each report is associated with exactly one post or comment being reported. This table may be referenced by discussion_board_report_of_citizens and discussion_board_report_of_moderators via 1:1 relationships.

foreignFields.name: reported_post_id
foreignFields.description: The post being reported. {@link discussion_board_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: reported_comment_id
foreignFields.description: The comment being reported. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: The type of actor who initiated the report. Must be either "citizen" or "moderator". This discriminates which subtype table contains the actor-specific details.

plainFields.name: complaint_reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the reporter for this report. This field is mandatory when reported by a citizen. When a moderator initiates a report, this field may contain an internal note.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The current status of this report. Values: "pending" (awaiting review), "dismissed" (investigation concluded with no violation), "edited" (content was edited after report), "deleted" (content was deleted after report). This status guides moderator workflows and audit trails.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the report was created and submitted.

models.name: discussion_board_report_of_citizens
models.description: Subtype entity for reports initiated by citizens. This table contains citizen-specific information about the report as part of the Polymorphic Ownership Pattern. There is a 1:1 relationship with the main discussion_board_reports entity. Each citizen-initiated report is uniquely associated with one citizen who reported it and one main report entity. This schema ensures referential integrity by eliminating the nullable actor foreign key anti-pattern in the main table.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_report_id
foreignFields.description: The main report entity this citizen report belongs to. {@link discussion_board_reports.id}.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who submitted this report. {@link discussion_board_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the citizen submitted this report, recorded separately for audit and timestamp accuracy.

models.name: discussion_board_report_of_moderators
models.description: Subtype entity for reports initiated by moderators. This table contains moderator-specific information about the report as part of the Polymorphic Ownership Pattern. There is a 1:1 relationship with the main discussion_board_reports entity. Each moderator-initiated report is uniquely associated with one moderator who reported it and one main report entity. This schema ensures referential integrity by eliminating the nullable actor foreign key anti-pattern in the main table. Note: Moderators can initiate reports for internal audit purposes without awaiting a citizen report.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_report_id
foreignFields.description: The main report entity this moderator report belongs to. {@link discussion_board_reports.id}.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who initiated this report. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the moderator initiated this report, recorded separately for audit and timestamp accuracy.

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_actions
models.description: Main entity capturing the audit event of a moderation action performed by a moderator. This is the central record that stores the action type, reason, timestamp, and discriminator for the moderated entity. Each moderation event (edit or delete) is a discrete business transaction. References to specific moderated entities (posts, comments, attachments) are handled through subsidiary tables to ensure referential integrity and compliance with 3NF normalization. This is NOT a standalone table; it must be joined with one of the three *_of_* subsidiary tables to determine what exactly was moderated. Use this table to count total moderation actions or filter by action_type. @link discussion_board_moderation_action_of_posts, @link discussion_board_moderation_action_of_comments, @link discussion_board_moderation_action_of_attachments

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who performed this moderation action. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of moderation action performed. Must be exactly 'edit' or 'delete'. This field is required to distinguish between modifications and removals in the audit trail.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Optional textual reason provided by the moderator for the moderation action. When a moderator actions follows a report, this field may capture the report reason. This complements the audit trail.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was performed. This is the moment the action was recorded. Always required.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this moderation record was last updated. Will be equal to created_at unless the moderation action is later updated (rare). Used for consistency tracking.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete marker. Only set if the moderation action itself is flagged as invalid (e.g., if a moderator overruled their own action). This preserves the audit trail but hides it from normal queries.

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_action_of_posts
models.description: Subsidiary table that links a specific moderation action to the post that was moderated. This table ensures referential integrity between moderation events and posts. Each row represents one moderation action applied to one post. Cannot exist without a parent in discussion_board_moderation_actions. This table only contains the FK to the moderated post and the parent moderation action. Used for querying all moderation actions on posts. @link discussion_board_moderation_actions

foreignFields.name: moderation_action_id
foreignFields.description: The moderation action record this subsidiary entry belongs to. {@link discussion_board_moderation_actions.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_post_id
foreignFields.description: The specific post that was moderated. This FK is non-nullable and enforce referential integrity with the discussion_board_posts table. {@link discussion_board_posts.id}

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_action_of_comments
models.description: Subsidiary table that links a specific moderation action to the comment that was moderated. This table ensures referential integrity between moderation events and comments. Each row represents one moderation action applied to one comment. Cannot exist without a parent in discussion_board_moderation_actions. This table only contains the FK to the moderated comment and the parent moderation action. Used for querying all moderation actions on comments. @link discussion_board_moderation_actions

foreignFields.name: moderation_action_id
foreignFields.description: The moderation action record this subsidiary entry belongs to. {@link discussion_board_moderation_actions.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: The specific comment that was moderated. This FK is non-nullable and enforce referential integrity with the discussion_board_comments table. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_action_of_attachments
models.description: Subsidiary table that links a specific moderation action to the attachment that was moderated. This table ensures referential integrity between moderation events and attachments. Each row represents one moderation action applied to one attachment. Cannot exist without a parent in discussion_board_moderation_actions. This table only contains the FK to the moderated attachment and the parent moderation action. Used for querying all moderation actions on attachments. @link discussion_board_moderation_actions

foreignFields.name: moderation_action_id
foreignFields.description: The moderation action record this subsidiary entry belongs to. {@link discussion_board_moderation_actions.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: The specific attachment that was moderated. This FK is non-nullable and enforce referential integrity with the discussion_board_attachments table. {@link discussion_board_attachments.id}
